Oct 7 MoE mix grid (three full-length Qwen3.6-35B-A3B runs, same recipe, one seed each): the T2.1-mix MoE leads on paper-edit small edits (0.63), long AI sections, the Fable humanizer set and standalone rewrites; mix A (AI-heavy) leads on clean v2 (+3.0 points) and is better calibrated; mix B (human-heavy) is last and over-flags human text (threshold 0.17). Details: MoE Mix Grid Results.

Recommendation: the T2.1 mix with original (hard) labels; MoE as the backbone if H200 time allows, otherwise the 4B. Soft labels give no clear gain, and the MoE leads the 4B on held-out and cross-model text (one MoE seed).

Soft labels (3 seeds each, paired): at a matched 1% FPR on each set’s own human controls, the soft arm is worse on clean v2 (0.72 vs 0.84; Opus 0.64 vs 0.85, Sonnet 0.71 vs 0.89; GPT-6 Sol and 6.1 Sol +3 and +5 points) and on the Fable humanizer set (0.61 vs 0.83), slightly better on held-out small edits (0.51 vs 0.48) and long AI sections (0.93 vs 0.92), and level on Fable co-writing. On paper-edit test small edits it is −4.9 points [−11, +1]. Its paper thresholds are much lower (0.23–0.31 against about 0.41), so at the paper threshold it flags more AI text and more human text (control FPR +0.4 to +1.0 points on every out-of-domain set); recall at that threshold overstates it. The losses sit on rewrites, where soft labels call copied clauses human but these evaluation sets label the whole rewritten span AI, so part of the gap is the label convention rather than detection.

T2.1 matches T2, so T2’s evidence carries over. On the paper-edit small edits the paired difference is −2.7 points on the test half [−8.2, +2.4] and −0.4 on dev [−3.4, +3.1]. Held-out AUROC is the same (0.953 vs 0.954). Seed 3 of T2.1 scores human text higher (paper threshold 0.67 vs about 0.41), which lowers its recall at the threshold but not its ranking.

SPG’s lead on the old small edits is home advantage. Those edits are all GPT-6 Luna rewrites, the writer of SPG’s splices. On clean v2, which has no Luna, T2.1 catches 79% of AI sentences against SPG’s 38% on the same rows, ahead for every writer and source, at a similar human false-positive rate (1.1% vs 0.9% of control sentences).

Cross-model human false positives: on the 500-document sample, T2.1 flags 0.56% of whole-human-document sentences against 0.27% for SPG (+0.29 points, interval [+0.04, +0.60]) and 0.63% for T2. A small cost, well below the 1% target.

Hardest cases on clean v2: Claude Fable 5.1 (69% of sentences; it is in no training mix) and arXiv hosts (67%). Fable light polish is flagged in 28% of documents against 7% of human documents; co-writing in 37% against 5%.

Backbone (old sets, T2 mix): the 20%-length MoE (one seed) is level with the 4B on paper-edit small edits (0.47 vs 0.48) and ahead on held-out writers (0.63 vs 0.60), long AI sections (0.91 vs 0.83) and standalone rewrites (0.85 vs 0.78); on that sample it flags 0.75% of whole-human-document sentences against 0.63% for the 4B, and 2.5% against 1.7% of all human sentences, most of them beside AI sections.
